Job Interview Checklist

Interviews reward preparation more than raw talent — the candidate who researched the company and rehearsed their stories almost always comes across better. This checklist takes you from research through the interview itself to the follow-up, so nothing catches you off guard. See more work checklists.

verified Curated by the Gisti team · Updated July 2026

Job Interview Checklist · 16 items

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Research the company: what it sells, recent news, and its mission

    Enough to explain why you want to work there specifically.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Re-read the job description and match your experience to each requirement
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Prepare stories for common questions using the STAR method

    Situation, Task, Action, Result — keeps answers concrete.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Prepare three to five thoughtful questions to ask the interviewer

    Not asking any reads as a lack of interest.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Look up your interviewers on LinkedIn if you know their names
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Practice a clear, confident introduction out loud
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Choose and lay out your outfit the night before
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Print several copies of your resume and a list of references
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Bring a notepad, pen, and any portfolio or work samples that fit the role
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Confirm the date, time, format, and location or video link

    Know whether it's in person, phone, or video.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Plan your route to arrive ten to fifteen minutes early

    For a video interview, test your camera, mic, and link ahead of time.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Prepare a salary range you'd accept, in case it comes up
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Silence your phone and bring a bottle of water
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Have questions ready about next steps and the timeline
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Send a short, specific thank-you email within 24 hours

    Reference something you actually discussed.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Write down notes right after, while the details are fresh

Frequently asked questions

How do I prepare for a job interview? expand_more

Research the company and role, then prepare STAR-method stories for common questions like your strengths, a challenge you handled, and why you want the job. Rehearse your introduction out loud, prepare questions to ask, and sort the logistics — outfit, route, copies of your resume — the night before. Preparation is what separates a calm interview from a stressful one.

What questions should I ask in an interview? expand_more

Ask about the role's day-to-day, what success looks like in the first few months, the team you'd join, and why the position is open. Good questions show you're serious and help you judge whether the job fits you. Avoid asking only about salary and time off in a first interview — save some of that for later stages.

Should I send a thank-you email after an interview? expand_more

Yes. Send a short, specific note within 24 hours thanking the interviewer and referencing something you discussed. It reinforces your interest and keeps you memorable, and surprisingly few candidates do it. Keep it to a few sentences — a genuine, concise message beats a long one.
